quests.scene: Someone who hurt you significantly offers you an apology. How do you respond?
options: Don't do it again.
I appreciate the apology. This genuinely affected me and I need a little time to process it properly.
Fine whatever.
Apology fully accepted. (immediately with no further discussion)
quests.hint: You can accept an apology while still honestly acknowledging how it affected you.
quests.explanation: I appreciate the apology. This genuinely affected me is emotionally honest.

quests.scene: A job interviewer asks: Why did you leave your previous position?
options: My previous manager was genuinely terrible.
The company had some very serious internal problems.
I was looking for new challenges and a stronger environment to develop. This role felt like exactly the right next step.
I was let go.
quests.hint: Keep your reason forward-looking and positive - never criticise a previous employer.
quests.explanation: Framing departure as seeking growth and connecting it to this specific role is the professional approach.

quests.scene: A friend enthusiastically shares a project they're passionate about. You think it is not commercially viable.
options: That will never work commercially.
How exciting! Have you tested the market for this yet?
I would definitely invest in this!
What made you think of that idea?
quests.hint: Encourage their passion while naturally introducing a practical and important question.
quests.explanation: How exciting! Have you tested the market yet? validates their enthusiasm and naturally introduces commercial thinking.

quests.scene: Your team achieves a major shared goal. Your manager publicly thanks the team. You respond:
options: Accept all the credit on behalf of the team.
Immediately list every team member's individual contributions publicly.
Thank you - this was a real team effort. Everyone brought so much to this.
Say nothing and let the manager continue.
quests.hint: Share the credit generously when success genuinely belongs to the whole team.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging that this was a team effort is generous and builds a strong trusting team culture.

quests.scene: You are facilitating a discussion and one person is clearly dominating the entire conversation.
options: Let them continue - their ideas are strong.
Tell them directly to stop talking so much.
Great points - I want to make sure we hear from everyone here. [Name] what is your view on this?
Ignore the dynamic and let the meeting run over.
quests.hint: Redirect the floor inclusively without silencing or embarrassing the dominant speaker.
quests.explanation: Thanking the dominant speaker and explicitly inviting others is inclusive facilitation.

quests.scene: A colleague privately shares that they are struggling with their mental health.
options: Immediately share your own mental health story with them.
Tell others so that more people can support them.
Listen without interrupting then ask: Thank you for trusting me with this. How can I best support you?
Recommend they see a doctor right away.
quests.hint: Listen first. Ask how they want to be supported - don't assume you know.
quests.explanation: Thanking them for their trust and asking how they prefer to be supported puts them in control.

quests.scene: You are writing a formal letter of complaint about poor service. What is the best opening?
options: You have made me very angry.
I am writing regarding a matter I experienced at your establishment on [specific date].
I want my money back.
This service was completely unacceptable.
quests.hint: Formal complaints should open with specific factual context - not emotion.
quests.explanation: Opening with the what where and when establishes context professionally before stating the complaint.

quests.scene: A friend constantly talks about their own problems but never asks how you are doing. You feel drained.
options: End the friendship immediately.
Say nothing and keep giving as much as you can.
Raise it honestly: I've noticed our conversations are mostly about your challenges. I find that tiring sometimes - could we try to be more balanced?
Vent extensively about your own problems to even things out.
quests.hint: Raise unequal emotional dynamics gently but with honest specificity.
quests.explanation: Naming the pattern and asking for balance is honest without being an attack.

quests.scene: A customer says loudly: This is the worst service I have ever experienced.
options: You are clearly overreacting.
I'm truly sorry to hear that. Could you help me understand what went wrong so I can make this right?
Other customers are genuinely satisfied with our service.
Let me pass you to my manager.
quests.hint: Apologise sincerely and seek to understand before offering any solution.
quests.explanation: An immediate genuine apology followed by a question de-escalates the situation.

quests.scene: You want to write a follow-up email after an unsuccessful job interview.
options: Demand detailed feedback from the company.
I wouldn't bother with that.
Dear [Name] Thank you for the interview opportunity. While I'm disappointed not to move forward I truly enjoyed learning about the team and would welcome any feedback.
Can I reapply for this same role immediately?
quests.hint: A gracious post-rejection email can open future doors with the organisation.
quests.explanation: Expressing gratitude acknowledging disappointment maturely and requesting feedback turns a rejection into a relationship-building moment.

quests.scene: You are asked to mediate a conflict between two colleagues who are not communicating.
options: Take the side of whoever you think is more right.
Let them work it out entirely on their own.
Meet with each of them privately first then bring them together when both feel heard.
Tell both of them they are both wrong.
quests.hint: Hear both sides separately before bringing them together.
quests.explanation: Meeting each person separately first allows them to speak freely without becoming defensive.

quests.scene: You have been asked to train a new colleague who will eventually take over your role.
options: Train them inadequately so they cannot replace you effectively.
Refuse to take on this responsibility.
Train them completely and with genuine generosity - their success reflects well on your training.
Train them but deliberately leave out important details and knowledge.
quests.hint: Your professionalism is never threatened by training someone else well.
quests.explanation: Training someone fully and generously demonstrates confidence and genuine professionalism.

quests.scene: You are presenting data to senior leadership and a board member says: I'm confused by this chart.
options: It's quite straightforward when you look carefully.
You're absolutely right - let me explain this more clearly. This shows [X] and the key takeaway is [Y].
The data speaks entirely for itself.
I'll send everyone a full clarification email afterward.
quests.hint: Accept the feedback immediately and make it clearer on the spot right now.
quests.explanation: Agreeing it was unclear and explaining it directly is the responsive confident move.

quests.scene: You are chairing a meeting and two participants begin arguing with each other.
options: Let them continue - it might resolve itself naturally.
Ask one of them to leave the meeting.
Let's take a moment - I'd like to hear both perspectives one at a time. Let's start with [name].
Adjourn the meeting immediately.
quests.hint: Restore structure calmly and give each person a fair organized chance to speak.
quests.explanation: Calling a pause and organizing the floor de-escalates the argument and restores the chair's authority.

quests.scene: You need to write a professional LinkedIn recommendation for a former colleague you genuinely respect.
options: I wouldn't really know what to write.
Keep it brief and generic: Great colleague and very hard worker.
Describe a specific situation where they excelled mention the measurable outcome and speak to their character.
Write extensively about yourself and mention them briefly.
quests.hint: Strong professional recommendations are always specific outcome-focused and authentic.
quests.explanation: A specific example with a concrete outcome is what makes a recommendation genuinely credible and useful.

quests.scene: You are working from home and your internet fails during an important client call.
options: Wait and hope the connection restores itself.
Email the client immediately: I'm very sorry - my internet dropped. Can I call you back at [number] in five minutes?
Try repeatedly to reconnect without any communication.
Reschedule by email later in the day.
quests.hint: Communicate immediately through an alternative channel.
quests.explanation: Sending an immediate email with a clear specific plan minimises disruption and demonstrates professionalism.

quests.scene: A job seeker asks your advice on how to negotiate a salary offer. What is the most effective guidance?
options: Never ask for more than whatever they initially offer you.
Always ask for exactly thirty percent more than any offer you receive.
Research market rates for your specific role and experience level then make a clear evidenced counter-offer.
Simply accept the first offer you receive and be grateful.
quests.hint: Effective salary negotiation is always based on research and clear reasoning.
quests.explanation: A counter-offer based on specific market data demonstrates preparation professionalism and genuine confidence.

quests.scene: You are about to give feedback to someone who has asked for it but appears emotionally fragile.
options: Give the harshest possible feedback - it builds real resilience.
Give only positive feedback even when it is not accurate.
Be completely honest but also compassionate - deliver any criticism gently followed by specific and actionable suggestions.
Postpone the feedback indefinitely.
quests.hint: Effective feedback is simultaneously honest AND considerate of the person's emotional state.
quests.explanation: Honest + compassionate + actionable is the formula for feedback that genuinely helps.

quests.scene: Your company's social media account receives a serious public criticism online.
options: Delete the comment immediately.
Respond publicly with a defensive tone.
Respond publicly: Thank you for raising this. We take it seriously and would like to speak with you directly - please contact us at [email].
Ignore it entirely and hope it disappears.
quests.hint: Public criticism requires a professional public response that redirects to private resolution.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging the concern publicly and redirecting to a private channel is the professional social media standard.

quests.scene: You have made the decision to resign from your current position. How do you tell your manager?
options: Send a brief resignation email and do not follow up.
Announce it immediately without any preparation.
Request a private meeting and say: I wanted to speak with you directly. I've decided to move on to a new role and I want to give you proper notice.
Tell your colleagues before telling your manager.
quests.hint: Resign directly privately and professionally - always tell your manager first.
quests.explanation: Telling your manager first in person and in private with proper notice is the professional approach.

quests.scene: During a critical negotiation the other party goes completely silent after your last point.
options: Fill the silence immediately with additional concessions.
Walk out of the negotiation.
Remain comfortable in the silence and wait for them to speak next.
Repeat your last offer or position again.
quests.hint: Silence in negotiation often creates productive pressure - resist filling it.
quests.explanation: Staying silent after making your point is a skilled negotiation tactic. Whoever fills the silence first is typically in the weaker position.

quests.scene: You have discovered a salary gap between yourself and a peer doing equivalent work. You want to discuss it with your manager.
options: Demand a raise immediately based solely on fairness.
I've been reflecting on my contributions and have also reviewed market rates. I'd value a conversation about my compensation.
I know exactly what [colleague] earns and I want the same.
Complain directly to HR without speaking to your manager first.
quests.hint: Frame the conversation around your value and market evidence - not colleague comparisons.
quests.explanation: Referencing your own contributions and market data keeps the conversation professional and based on your own merit.

quests.scene: A new team member is consistently underperforming. As their peer what is the most appropriate first step?
options: Report them to the manager immediately.
Do their work for them to protect the project.
Cover for them publicly without addressing it.
Offer privately: I've noticed you seem to be struggling with [specific task]. I've been there myself - would you like to work through it together?
quests.hint: Specific private peer support is the most effective first response to performance difficulties.
quests.explanation: Offering specific private help builds genuine trust and often resolves performance issues before they require escalation.

quests.scene: You are at a business dinner and the conversation naturally lulls. What do you do?
options: Sit in silence and wait for the other person to speak.
Begin talking at length about yourself.
Check your phone to fill the time.
Ask: What's a project you're most proud of this year? or What is the most interesting development in your sector right now?
quests.hint: Great conversationalists ask thoughtful questions that genuinely invite engagement.
quests.explanation: Open interest-based questions are natural engaging and demonstrate genuine curiosity.

quests.scene: You are travelling and the exchange rate at the currency office seems lower than expected.
options: Accept the first rate you encounter.
Exchange your money at every bureau you see.
Say politely: Is that your best available rate? I've seen better rates elsewhere - is there any flexibility?
Complain loudly and publicly about the rate.
quests.hint: Politely questioning the rate is completely normal and often surprisingly effective.
quests.explanation: Asking whether the rate is negotiable and mentioning you've seen better rates elsewhere is a reasonable polite way to seek a better deal.

quests.scene: Your neighbour plays loud music late at night repeatedly. You have never spoken to them.
options: Call the police immediately on first occurrence.
Leave an angry anonymous note under their door.
Knock on their door: Hi I'm [name] from [flat number]. I don't think we've actually met. I wanted to have a friendly chat about the noise in the evenings - is now a good moment?
Suffer in complete silence.
quests.hint: A direct calm neighbourly conversation is always the right first step.
quests.explanation: Introducing yourself properly and using a conversational tone shows respect and gives the neighbour every chance to resolve this amicably.

quests.scene: You are asked to peer review a colleague's academic paper that has significant structural weaknesses.
options: Reject it with a single brief note.
Approve it without comment to preserve the relationship.
Send only positive feedback with an encouraging note.
Provide structured feedback on both genuine strengths and specific areas that need development.
quests.hint: Academic peer review requires rigour balance and constructive specificity.
quests.explanation: A peer review should identify authentic strengths alongside specific weaknesses and suggestions for improvement.

quests.scene: Your colleague is presenting in their second language and the audience is visibly impatient.
options: Take over the presentation from them mid-sentence.
Make encouraging eye contact nod supportively and if appropriate clarify a key point gently after they have finished.
Ask someone else to translate for them.
Pass them a note asking them to speak faster.
quests.hint: Be a supportive presence without ever undermining their confidence or authority.
quests.explanation: Encouraging eye contact and gentle clarification after they finish supports them without taking over.

quests.scene: A client asks you for a professional reference but you know the role they are applying for is not a good fit for them.
options: Provide the reference and say absolutely nothing else.
Decline to write any reference at all.
Provide the reference but also have an honest private conversation: I'll give you a strong reference. I also want to share one honest observation - just for your benefit.
Tell the hiring company your concerns without asking the client.
quests.hint: A reference and a private honest conversation are not mutually exclusive.
quests.explanation: Giving the reference while sharing private caring feedback respects the client's autonomy while fulfilling your duty to be honest.

quests.scene: You discover your team has been cutting corners on quality standards in order to meet a tight deadline.
options: Ignore it - the deadline was successfully met after all.
Punish the team formally.
Address it immediately: understand what pressure drove it acknowledge the difficulty and set clear expectations going forward.
Report it to senior leadership without speaking to the team first.
quests.hint: Understanding the root cause is just as important as addressing the visible behaviour.
quests.explanation: Understanding why corners were cut allows you to fix the systemic cause rather than just the symptoms.
